column1: # zengif find_nearest branchless-chunked-min optimization — ARM A/B (FALSIFIED)
# Box: Hetzner cax21, ARM Neoverse-N1 (aarch64), 4 cores, 7.5 GB RAM
# Toolchain: cargo 1.96.0; RUSTFLAGS='' (runtime SIMD dispatch, NO target-cpu=native)
# Method: ONE source tree, src/types.rs swapped between scalar baseline and the
#   branchless chunked (dist<<8)|index running-min, each phase recompiled
#   (17.65s baseline / 17.93s optimized; on-box marker chunks_exact 0 vs 1).
# Raw log: zen-arm-results/zengif/zengif_arm_bench_FINAL.log (off-repo).
# NOTE: zenbench reported "0 rounds" (single-shot, no statistical rounds) so each
# number is one measurement — but the regression is far outside noise and
# directionally consistent across the two solid/full-frame encode paths.
# VERDICT: NOT A WIN. The optimization REGRESSES the dominant encode/solid path
# ~30% and helps the dirty-region animation path only ~2-3%. Reverted on main.
# Correctness was byte-identical (see *_correctness_*.tsv); this is purely a
# performance falsification.
# bench(ms)
encode/solid/256x256x10
encode/solid/512x512x10
memory_allocation/encode/512x512x50
animation_stress/encode/512x512x200_dirty32
animation_stress/encode/512x512x200_dirty64
animation_stress/encode/512x512x200_dirty128
animation_stress/encode/512x512x200_dirty256
# --- control: decode (no find_nearest), unchanged within noise ---
decode/solid/256x256x10
decode/solid/512x512x10
decode/solid/1024x1024x10
decode/transparent/512x512x10
# Likely root cause: solid/near-solid frames hit an exact palette match at a low
# index, so the scalar loop's `dist==0` early-exit returns after ~1 comparison;
# the chunked-min must finish a full 8-entry chunk before it can early-exit, doing
# MORE work on the common case. The isolated x86 microbench (1.1-1.17x) did not
# predict this. A future attempt should keep a fast per-element `dist==0` exit
# (e.g. probe index 0 / a small scalar prefix before the vector body) and re-bench.
